biological.citation: A Novel De Novo Gain-of-Function CACNA1D Variant in Neurodevelopmental Disease With Congenital Tremor, Seizures, and Hypotonia (PMID: 39246741)
biological.summary: Patch-clamp electrophysiology of the p.(G1169D) CACNA1D variant in tsA201 cells revealed pronounced activity-enhancing gating changes, including shifts of channel activation and inactivation to more hyperpolarized potentials, as well as impaired channel inactivation and deactivation. This gain-of-function variant was identified de novo in two children with neurodevelopmental disease of variable severity. The variant retained sensitivity to the Ca2+ channel blocker isradipine in vitro, though no beneficial clinical effects were observed.

biological.citation: CACNA1D-Related Channelopathies: From Hypertension to Autism (PMID: 36592224)
biological.summary: CACNA1D encodes the pore-forming α1 subunit of Cav1.3 L-type voltage-gated Ca2+ channels; loss of function causes deafness and bradycardia, while de novo gain-of-function missense variants cause a neurodevelopmental syndrome including autism spectrum disorder, epilepsy, primary aldosteronism, and hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia. In vitro electrophysiological studies of multiple de novo variants revealed activity-enhancing gating changes consistent with enhanced Ca2+ influx as the disease mechanism. Dihydropyridine L-type Ca2+ channel blockers have been explored as potential therapeutic options.

biological.citation: CACNA1D overexpression and voltage-gated calcium channels in prostate cancer during androgen deprivation (PMID: 36949059)
biological.summary: CACNA1D and CaV1.3 protein are overexpressed in prostate tumours; in androgen-sensitive LNCaP cells, androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) or enzalutamide treatment increased CACNA1D expression and enabled depolarization/Bay K 8644-evoked nifedipine-sensitive Ca2+ transients and detectable CaV1.3 currents. CACNA1D knockdown reduced the subpopulation of treated LNCaP cells with CaV1.3 activity. These findings suggest that physiological and genomic CACNA1D/CaV1.3 mechanisms become active during hormone therapy in prostate cancer.

biological.citation: Nutrient-sensitizing drug repurposing screen identifies lomerizine as a mitochondrial metabolism inhibitor of chronic myeloid leukemia (PMID: 38865484)
biological.summary: Transcriptome analysis revealed increased expression of voltage-gated CACNA1D in CML leukemic stem cells (CD34+CD38-) compared with normal counterparts, correlating with increased ER mass and elevated ER and mitochondrial Ca2+ content. CACNA1D knockdown in CML cells led to ER and mitochondrial Ca2+ depletion, inhibited mitochondrial isocitrate dehydrogenase activity, and sensitized CML LSCs to imatinib treatment. These findings implicate CACNA1D-mediated Ca2+ influx in supporting mitochondrial oxidative metabolism in CML stem cells.

biological.citation: Dominant role of CACNA1D exon mutations for blood pressure regulation (PMID: 35142739)
biological.summary: CRISPR-Cas9-engineered Sprague-Dawley rats carrying the CACNA1D p.D307G mutation showed elevated systolic blood pressure, increased circulating ET-1, and vascular/cardiac/renal remodeling over 32 weeks. Increased Cav1.3 protein expression and calcineurin phosphatase activity were observed in VSMCs, and ET-1 expression was elevated in aortic endothelial cells from mutant rats. Double heterozygosity (p.D307G/p.R1516Q or p.D307G/p.V936I) further accelerated SBP rise, and isradipine or BQ-123 reduced BP in double-mutant rats.

biological.citation: CaBP1 and 2 enable sustained CaV1.3 calcium currents and synaptic transmission in inner hair cells (PMID: 39718549)
biological.summary: In Cabp1/2 double-knockout mice, CaV1.3 (encoded by CACNA1D) showed strongly enhanced inactivation, slowed recovery from inactivation, and impaired sustained exocytosis at inner hair cell ribbon synapses. Spontaneous and sound-evoked responses of spiral ganglion neurons were strikingly reduced, demonstrating that CaBP1 and CaBP2 cooperatively suppress voltage- and calcium-dependent inactivation of IHC CaV1.3 channels to support fast, temporally precise sound encoding. Transgenic expression of CaBP2 substantially rescued IHC synaptic function and hearing sensitivity.

Somatic driver mutations in CACNA1D (encoding the α1 subunit of L-type voltage-gated calcium channel CaV1.3) are found in a substantial portion of aldosterone-producing adenomas, implicating intracellular calcium signaling as a key pathway in aldosterone overproduction. Rare germline variants of CACNA1D have also been reported in familial hyperaldosteronism. These mutations lead to altered ion transport, cell membrane depolarization, activation of voltage-gated calcium channels, and increased aldosterone synthase transcription.

biological.citation: ASHG 2017 - African ancestry genome- and transcriptome-wide association study of blood pressure detects nine novel loci in a large cohort from the Million Veteran Program
biological.summary: In the largest single-cohort GWAS of African Americans (N~59,900), the most significant SNP for diastolic blood pressure after meta-analysis with COGENT BP Consortium data was at the CACNA1D locus (p-value = 1.26×10-12). This finding identifies CACNA1D as a novel locus for diastolic blood pressure in African Americans. Transcriptome-wide association analysis suggested that reduced expression of nearby TMEM110 in nucleus accumbens-basal ganglia may be the relevant functional signal for the SBP association in that region.

biological.citation: ASHG 2015 - Epigenomic profiling of prostate cancer identifies differentially methylated genes in TMPRSS2:ERG fusion positive versus negative tumors
biological.summary: In a population-based cohort of 496 prostate cancer patients, CACNA1D was among the top 25 differentially methylated CpGs (FDR ≤1.53×10-29) between TMPRSS2:ERG fusion-positive and fusion-negative tumors. CACNA1D showed gene body hypomethylation and mRNA overexpression in fusion-positive prostate cancer, and is described as a known ERG target gene. These findings suggest CACNA1D is epigenetically regulated downstream of the T2E fusion and may represent a therapeutic target.

biological.citation: ASHG 2014 - Exome analyses reveal new autism genes in synaptic, transcriptional, and chromatin networks
biological.summary: Whole-exome sequencing of 3,871 autism cases and 9,937 controls identified CACNA1D (encoding the Ca2+ channel CaV1.3) among 107 high-confidence ASD risk genes enriched for de novo loss-of-function mutations (FDR<0.30). CACNA1D was specifically highlighted as a critical synaptic gene involved in neuronal pacemaking and excitability-transcription coupling. The study implicated synaptic development as a major theme in ASD risk, with CACNA1D as a key voltage-gated ion channel component.
